newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA RAISES FUEL PRICES FOR JANUARY 22-34 PCT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA RAISES FUEL PRICES FOR JANUARY 22-34 PCT.

text.p: Bulgaria's outgoing cabinet raised petrol and diesel fuel prices for January by 22 and 34 percent respectively, state news agency BTA said.
Petrol prices depending on the grade rose to 208-276 levs per litre from 171-226 levs and price of diesel gained to 189 levs per litre from 141, effective from January 1, BTA said.
The decision on the rise was taken at a closed door cabinet meeting on Sunday under a pricing mechanism for a monthly update of fuel prices in line with inflation and the lev/dollar exchange rate.
The Bulgarian lev fell to 500-502 to the dollar on Monday from around 354 at the beginning of December.
Monthly inflation for December was expected to be 15 percent and cumulative inflation for 1996 was seen near 270 percent, local media quoted experts as saying.
In January when the lev traded at around 70 per dollar, average petrol prices were 27.25 levs per litre and the diesel fuel price was 19.50 per litre.
Fuel prices include value added tax of 22 percent. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
